exact_asset.title: Artemis I Launches to the Moon (Official NASA Recap)
exact_asset.excerpt: NASA Image and Video Library catalog record for the exact 151.57-second source asset used in this project.

nasa_media.title: NASA Images and Media Usage Guidelines
nasa_media.excerpt: NASA says its content generally is not subject to copyright in the United States, but factual use must not imply endorsement; identifiable people and marked third-party material require separate attention.

nasa_brand.title: NASA Brand Guidelines
nasa_brand.excerpt: NASA states that its Insignia, Logotype, identifiers, and imagery are not in the public domain and directs brand questions to agency-brand@nasa.gov.

nasa_film.title: NASA Film and Documentary Guidelines
nasa_film.excerpt: NASA distinguishes use of publicly available footage from requests for agency participation, location access, identifier clearance, or production assistance.

artemis_mission.title: Artemis I
artemis_mission.excerpt: NASA identifies Artemis I as the first integrated flight test of Orion, the Space Launch System, and upgraded Exploration Ground Systems at Kennedy Space Center.

pad_39b.title: Launch Pad 39B
pad_39b.excerpt: NASA’s facility page identifies Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center and records its support of the Artemis I mission.

bill_nelson.title: Bill Nelson — NASA Administrator, May 2021–January 2025
bill_nelson.excerpt: NASA’s biography confirms Bill Nelson’s identity and dates of service as the agency’s fourteenth administrator.

esa_orion.title: ESA — Orion spacecraft
esa_orion.excerpt: ESA states that it provides Orion’s European Service Module, supplying electricity, propulsion, thermal control, air, and water.

candidate_rights_holders.name: NASA Office of Communications
candidate_rights_holders.role: administrator of NASA identifiers and brand guidance
candidate_rights_holders.basis: NASA’s current brand guidance identifies the insignia and official identifiers as protected and supplies a brand contact.

licensing_routes.route: Request brand-usage guidance for the intended edit and distribution context.

NASA insignia.research_summary: The underlying NASA footage is generally available for factual use, but NASA treats its insignia and identifiers separately. The edit should preserve source attribution, avoid endorsement implications, and receive human review against the intended release context.
evidence_gaps: The project’s commercial, promotional, and merchandising contexts are not yet recorded.
unresolved_questions: Will the insignia appear only within the unaltered source footage, or also in marketing and key art?
recommended_actions: Send the intended use, frame grabs, territories, and media plan to NASA’s brand contact for written guidance.
NASA insignia.public_domain_status: NASA-produced footage is generally not subject to U.S. copyright, but the NASA insignia and identifiers are expressly treated as protected.
NASA insignia.known_disputes: No dispute was identified in the reviewed official sources.

candidate_rights_holders.name: NASA Office of Communications
candidate_rights_holders.role: administrator of NASA mission and campaign identifiers
candidate_rights_holders.basis: The identity appears in NASA’s own asset and NASA’s brand framework covers mission and campaign identifiers.

licensing_routes.route: Submit the featured Artemis identity use for brand-guidance review.

Artemis mission identity.research_summary: The Artemis identity is a featured graphic element, not merely incidental launch footage. NASA’s mission page verifies the subject; its brand guidance is the controlling public route for identifier questions.
evidence_gaps: No written confirmation covers the identity’s use outside the original NASA recap.
unresolved_questions: Will the edit reproduce or alter the Artemis identity in titles, thumbnails, or advertising?
recommended_actions: Separate in-footage use from any newly created Artemis-branded graphics and obtain written guidance for the latter.
Artemis mission identity.public_domain_status: The public availability of the mission footage does not establish unrestricted use of the mission identity.
Artemis mission identity.known_disputes: None identified in the reviewed official sources.

candidate_rights_holders.name: NASA Kennedy Space Center
candidate_rights_holders.role: federal facility depicted in the source footage
candidate_rights_holders.basis: NASA’s facility page verifies the location and its relationship to Artemis I.

licensing_routes.route: Confirm whether the intended use is limited to public archival footage or requests additional location participation.

Launch Pad 39B.research_summary: Launch Pad 39B is verified as the NASA facility shown in the recap. Reusing NASA’s published footage is a different clearance path from filming or obtaining production assistance on NASA property.
evidence_gaps: The production has not stated whether it seeks only archival use or additional facility access.
unresolved_questions: Are any newly shot Kennedy Space Center exteriors or interiors planned?
recommended_actions: Document that this cut uses the exact public asset; route any new location request through NASA Entertainment Collaborations.
Launch Pad 39B.public_domain_status: Location facts are public; footage and agency participation remain subject to NASA’s published conditions.

candidate_rights_holders.name: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
candidate_rights_holders.role: publisher and stated source of the selected recap asset
candidate_rights_holders.share: NASA-produced asset; third-party components not itemized
candidate_rights_holders.basis: The exact asset is cataloged by NASA and the agency’s media guidance states the general reuse framework.

licensing_routes.route: Retain the exact catalog record and request clarification for any marked or unidentified third-party material.
licensing_routes.contact: NASA Images and Media guidance portal

NASA Artemis I launch footage.research_summary: The project uses an exact, publicly cataloged NASA recap. NASA says agency content generally is not subject to U.S. copyright, while warning that identifiable people, protected identifiers, endorsement, and marked third-party content require separate review.
evidence_gaps: The public catalog record does not provide a component-level cue sheet or third-party-material schedule.
unresolved_questions: Does the selected edit retain any separately licensed music, graphics, or crowd material?
recommended_actions: Attach the catalog record, checksum, NASA usage guidance, and a frame-accurate usage log to the production packet.
NASA Artemis I launch footage.public_domain_status: Generally not subject to U.S. copyright as NASA content; exceptions and non-copyright restrictions remain possible.
NASA Artemis I launch footage.known_disputes: None identified in the catalog or reviewed guidance.

candidate_rights_holders.name: Bill Nelson
candidate_rights_holders.role: identifiable person appearing and speaking in the footage
rights_implicated: right of publicity or privacy depending on use
candidate_rights_holders.share: Personal rights are use- and jurisdiction-dependent
candidate_rights_holders.basis: NASA’s biography confirms the identity and term shown in the lower third; NASA’s media guidance flags identifiable-person issues for commercial use.

licensing_routes.organization: Production counsel / NASA Office of Communications
licensing_routes.route: Determine whether the factual excerpt needs a separate likeness release for the intended commercial and promotional contexts.

Bill Nelson.research_summary: Bill Nelson is clearly identifiable by face, voice, name, and his then-current NASA title. NASA’s official biography verifies the historical title, while the agency’s media guidance warns that commercial use involving identifiable people may require permission.
evidence_gaps: No release or use-specific consent is attached to the project.
unresolved_questions: Is the use editorial within the film only, or will Nelson’s image or quote appear in advertising, thumbnails, or merchandise?
recommended_actions: Have counsel assess the intended use and jurisdiction; request written direction before promotional use of the excerpt.
Bill Nelson.public_domain_status: Government footage status does not eliminate a separate likeness/publicity analysis.
Bill Nelson.known_disputes: None identified in the reviewed sources.

candidate_rights_holders.name: European Space Agency
candidate_rights_holders.role: provider of Orion’s European Service Module and official subject-matter source
candidate_rights_holders.share: Component source not itemized in NASA’s recap catalog
candidate_rights_holders.basis: ESA’s official Orion page confirms its role; the exact origin of each spacecraft shot in the NASA edit is not itemized.

licensing_routes.route: Confirm attribution and whether the selected Orion imagery includes ESA-supplied material with separate terms.

European Space Agency.research_summary: ESA is verified as the provider of Orion’s European Service Module. The NASA recap names and depicts the module, but its catalog does not identify the source agency for each spacecraft image or animation.
evidence_gaps: Shot-level image credits are absent from the public recap catalog record.
unresolved_questions: Which Orion shots or animations, if any, were supplied by ESA or an industrial partner?
recommended_actions: Request a shot-level credit confirmation and record the required NASA/ESA attribution in the packet.
European Space Agency.public_domain_status: Not established for any ESA-originated component; do not extend NASA’s U.S. government-media status by inference.

candidate_rights_holders.name: Unconfirmed soundtrack rights holder
candidate_rights_holders.role: composition and/or master owner not named in the public catalog record
candidate_rights_holders.basis: Music is audible throughout, while the exact NASA catalog record and official captions do not identify a cue, composer, publisher, or label.

licensing_routes.route: Request the recap’s cue sheet or written confirmation of soundtrack reuse rights before relying on the asset’s general media status.
licensing_routes.contact: NASA Images and Media guidance portal

Unidentified musical score.research_summary: The score is clearly audible but remains unidentified. NASA warns that third-party material may be used on its sites under permission that does not transfer to downstream users, so the music should remain red until provenance is documented.
evidence_gaps: No cue sheet, composer, publisher, label, or license scope was found in the public catalog record.
unresolved_questions: Was the music commissioned by NASA, placed under a transferable license, or licensed only for the original recap?
recommended_actions: Obtain a cue sheet or replace the soundtrack with production-controlled music before final delivery.
Unidentified musical score.public_domain_status: Unknown; do not infer that music is public domain from the government source of the surrounding footage.
Unidentified musical score.known_disputes: None researched because the work is not yet identified.

candidate_rights_holders.name: NASA Office of Communications
candidate_rights_holders.role: primary public contact for NASA identifiers visible in the visitor-area shot
candidate_rights_holders.share: Operator and apparel ownership not established
candidate_rights_holders.basis: NASA owns the agency identifier and verifies the location, but the public asset record does not identify every sign or garment operator.

licensing_routes.route: Provide the representative frame and ask whether any visitor-complex or third-party identifier needs separate routing.

Kennedy Space Center visitor signage.research_summary: NASA and Space Center identifiers are legible in a brief crowd shot. The agency brand route is established; ownership of every visitor-area sign and branded garment is not established from the footage alone.
evidence_gaps: No operator list or product-identification log is attached for the crowd shot.
unresolved_questions: Is the shot incidental enough for the intended edit, or will it be isolated in promotional frames?
recommended_actions: Retain the frame in the log, avoid promotional isolation, and route any featured use through NASA’s brand contact.
Kennedy Space Center visitor signage.public_domain_status: Not a public-domain determination; signage and identifiers require their own contextual review.
